Cadence: 
Every Wednesday either Under Review, Active, Tabled or Killed
Review top line notes (any red flags)  > one pager > scorecard
Overnight audit will shift to tabs & resort with Active at top
Pipeline partially worked. Warm intros needed. Conference Oct 2026.
HNW Personal Lines Concierge Insurance Brokerage

UNMERGE from Art Insurance. $106.6B HNW market, 11.9% CAGR, ~100% renewals. 20-40 indie brokerages. August Felker WARM 4mo stale w/ named targets. Strongest RTW in pipeline. RE-SCORED 5/19 -> 2.65 (+0.12) on Aug Felker 11/19 platonic-target evidence + Hunter 1/12 carve-out workaround.
Recurring retainers $2-15K/property/month. Zero PE activity. No association/directory. TAM too small for DealsX, strong for proprietary.

Asset-light SERVICES layer only (crating / fine-art trucking / installation / customs brokerage) — strips capital-intensive storage. 15-25% EBITDA, ~60% convertible recurring (referral-locked). ~4-5% CAGR, US services TAM $1-2B. Strongest net-new this cycle: Strong RTW + warm access (Warren Chan/Anacapa ~June 9). NOTE: services-only RE-SCOPE of tracked #8 Storage for HVA — Kay to decide re-scope vs net-new (do not double-count). Exit comps: UOVO, Crozier/Iron Mountain, Cadogan Tate.
Storage & Related Services for High Value Assets

Reactivated 4/19/2026 on Saltoun greenlight + AI cost-efficiency thesis. Multi-channel margin play (storage 16-40% gross). 8% blended baseline - demand abundant, cost is bottleneck. Prior LOI work: Acumen stalled, Hangman passed. Industry insight: outreach leads on ops/AI, not growth.
A2LA proxy: cosmetic 6 local records; perfume 1 local; broader chemical/microbiology records much larger

Niche-intelligence intake 7/8/26. Stronger if broadened from pure fragrance to cosmetic/fragrance product testing. A2LA proxy found 6 local cosmetic records and 1 local perfume record; broader chemical/microbiology records are larger but noisy. MoCRA/IFRA/EU allergen documentation are tailwinds. Folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1FaAIjSyM0aWLiBD51uXAsnkZBQycsvO4
A2LA proxy: packaging/package 13 local NY/NJ/CT records; ISTA 1 local record

Niche-intelligence intake 7/8/26. Strongest packaging lane. A2LA proxy found 13 local NY/NJ/CT packaging/package records and 1 local ISTA record. Repeat testing from launches, supplier changes, e-commerce transit, sustainability shifts, and quality failures. Folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1DfXLvmBQ1x16__o56OXhM64rcKDaxQJ3
Highly fragmented; small owner-run firms everywhere. PE wants 1000s-of-doors portfolios, not single-market firms. LI/NYC metro pool large.

Manage rental properties for owners (NOT HOA). Recurring mgmt fee ~8-12pct of rent + leasing + maintenance markup. PE: recent residential wave 2022+ (ProperXPM/TriSpan $100M, Alfred/RKW, Mynd/Roofstock) buying 1000s of doors, NOT chasing sub-$1M owners. MULTIPLES: small owner-run 2-3x SDE ($200-500/door); mid platform 5-7x EBITDA; tech-enabled 9-11x. WEAKNESS vs HOA: owner churn 15-25pct/yr, thinner margins, less sticky. Commercial PM = Big 3 (CBRE/JLL/Cushman) dominated, thin field. Cheap off-market lane: sub-$1M single-market residential 2-3x SDE.
Luxury Leather Goods, Handbag, Footwear, and Garment Aftercare Services
Likely yes, subject to structure and tax review

TEST, not Activate. Luxury repair/product-care circularity wedge. Validate premium target density, ownership/backing, B2B repeat revenue, EBITDA margins, technician capacity, and whether repair can scale without losing atelier trust. Folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/19YQlV4SQ7m2it3h-kT3c7GYHq0PwK3Xo
Luxury Amenity Management for Commercial/Residential Real Estate
30-100 independently owned acquisition candidates estimated; focused-to-long sprint.

Score 76/100 (2.28/3). Recurring B2B property-service niche with G&B luxury-service right-to-win and Arch/Flacks validation. One-pager: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1aXSMc3bPzPGGNieiWwVqJROdEK2Efjfk/edit?usp=drivesdk. Scorecard: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1zIIw_AbowIFUqxzb2C-CDZPkp1SOQ_oD/edit?usp=drivesdk. Red flags: labor intensity, wage inflation, safety/insurance incidents, customer concentration, proof of sub-Arch target pool.
Insurance-Driven Contents Restoration, Pack-Out, Inventory, and Storage Services
Likely QSBS-eligible if structured as operating services; verify storage/real-estate exposure.

Promising insurance-loss services wedge; strongest if contents-only, referral-heavy, low reconstruction mix. Watch carrier/TPA pricing power and franchise/PE roll-ups. Folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1MphKfR6D4oHsrzODLimC67KJnKIGAkwb
Asset-Light Boat and Yacht Transport Coordination for Marinas, Dealers, Brokers, and Seasonal Owners
75-250 independently owned haulers/coordinators estimated; scale above $750K EBITDA unproven.

Score 71/100 (2.13/3). Right-to-win and low visible PE saturation; best version is asset-light coordination/brokerage. One-pager: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1FQhqZ0Pijterw17sB2wrMlCbVOUUvVBX/edit?usp=drivesdk. Scorecard: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/11lxxLYK49ZpOc3YAg4K9QDA-GGNyNLyn/edit?usp=drivesdk. Red flags: weakly contractual revenue, seasonality, liability exposure, carrier power, unproven scaled target pool.
MoCRA-Compliant Beauty 3PL, Kitting, and Fulfillment for Independent Cosmetics Brands
Likely, subject to structure; avoid distribution-only inventory-heavy models
40-100 estimated independent targets; 25-75 with credible MoCRA/FDA/hazmat/climate-control positioning

Strong regulatory and beauty-infrastructure signal; target must be specialized fulfillment/kitting with real lot/traceability workflows, not generic 3PL or packaging/testing duplicate. Red flags: Generic 3PL margin compression; PE-backed logistics competition; MoCRA marketing claims may be shallow; overlap with existing beauty testing/packaging/distribution rows.
Yacht Property Management for Private Yacht Owners in Coastal HNW Markets
Likely, subject to structure; not a financial-services exclusion
75-150 estimated independent firms; many may be small captain-service shops

Ongoing yacht stewardship for HNW owners; recurring service behavior and professionalization levers are attractive. Main diligence is platform-scale target depth and captain/key-person dependency. Red flags: Thin platform-scale target pool; labor/key-person dependency; luxury-cycle exposure; strategic brokerages can bundle management.
TBD; packaging suppliers exist but scaled independent local targets unclear

Niche-intelligence intake 7/8/26. Conditional WATCH: luxury/beauty adjacency and repeat launches, but may be product/inventory/overseas-sourcing heavy rather than a recurring service platform. Needs target proof and working-capital screen. Folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1VhZwrixZHNzOvxfC_t3ekQ8OXV2p5v42
TBD; likely limited independent scaled targets

Niche-intelligence intake 7/8/26. Conditional WATCH: attractive only if specialty/value-added distributor with formulation, regulatory docs, sampling, inventory, and sticky repeat accounts. Plain distribution likely lower-margin/working-capital-heavy and consolidated by specialty chemical distributors. Folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1gjWXylpepmlgwMia0yW59WzHuMnIOTE-
Jeweler's Block Insurance Brokerage for Independent Jewelry Retailers, Wholesalers, and Pawn/Jewelry Trade Businesses
Unlikely / major caveat; insurance brokerage and financial-services exclusions need counsel review
20-40 estimated independent specialist targets; thin child wedge

Excellent recurring insurance economics and mission criticality, but target pool is thin and generic brokerage is heavily consolidated. Treat as specialty-insurance child wedge/watchlist unless proprietary access appears. Red flags: QSBS likely problematic; high PE/strategic consolidation; thin target pool; niche-only TAM/growth unvalidated; carrier/program power.
Trade Credit, Customs Bonds & Cargo Insurance Brokerage
200-500 trade-credit specialists + 3000 CBP customs brokers; tristate 100-200

Unified Trade-Risk Brokerage thesis (TABLED+KILLED resurface - bundled cross-sell fixes original unit-econ tabling). Jeremy Black bullish + Camilla research convergence. 20-35% EBITDA, 90%+ retention, 7-8% CAGR. CBP regulatory mandate.

Reconciliation row - Drive folder + scorecard + one-pager exist from 3/31 run (Katie Walker TX deal as warm intro), but row was never added to WEEKLY REVIEW. 25-40% EBITDA contingency-fee, 70%+ recurring, 7.1% CAGR. PE consolidation Medium.

Fragmented; 50-100+ independent NYC-metro benchmarking/audit firms (est). ~50K NYC bldgs under LL97. Named: Cotocon Group, IntelliGreen Partners (WOMEN-OWNED/WBE-Valerie Corbett), Partner Energy, Latitude Compliance.

NYC LL97/LL84/LL87 compliance: annual benchmarking (recurring) + energy audits/retrocommissioning + decarb planning (project). PASSES PE FILTER - consolidation only at TOP (Willdan, ICF, TRC buy $5M+ EBITDA platforms); small NYC owner-run shops BELOW PE radar (~8-10x at scale, small end cheaper/open). 2030 LL97 demand cliff (~57pct of bldgs projected over cap vs under 10pct now; $900M+/yr potential fines). Margins 10-20pct. WOMEN-OWNED target found (IntelliGreen). RISK: project lumpiness; single-jurisdiction NYC regulatory concentration. STRONGEST of the 5.
Stormwater Control Measure Inspection, Maintenance, and Compliance O&M for HOAs, Multifamily, Retail Centers, and Commercial Campuses
Likely Eligible; confirm service-heavy/non-construction structure with counsel
100-250 estimated independent stormwater O&M / SCM inspection and maintenance providers; validate 50+ buy-box-scale targets after excluding landscaping, engineering, and construction-heavy firms

Score 2.52/3.00. Regulatory stormwater O&M niche for HOAs, multifamily, retail centers, and commercial campuses. Tailwinds: MS4/NPDES maintenance obligations, flooding, aging stormwater assets, green infrastructure, HOA/commercial compliance. Recurring/reoccurring inspection, cleaning, reporting, repair cycles. PE risk medium/rising via Dragonfly/Warren, AQUALIS/Fusion, SWIMS/Apex, StormWater Pros/Silver Peak. Folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1YWvgpkdYQ5BDoUWmjVXSMglitObIcQ9t
Water/Wastewater SCADA & Controls Compliance Service Providers

Score 2.47/3.00. Narrowed water/wastewater SCADA, PLC/HMI, telemetry, instrumentation, cybersecurity, and compliance-support providers; excludes broad electrical construction, pump/equipment distribution, and one-off plant construction. PASS initial screen; 5.5-13pct growth proxies, $1.89B+ SCADA/smart-water TAM. Key diligence: recurring support/calibration/emergency/cybersecurity revenue mix vs. project integration and equipment pass-through. Folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1bWAHoFr8C9BriAmM4ksMXZ61Fm18JLb_
~90% of $54B mkt = small independents; ~365K US associations; LI/NYC metro 100+ small firms (Einsidler ~70 communities, LIMS, Touchstone, Quantum, HMH, Destiny)

Buy the for-profit MANAGER not the nonprofit HOA. Recurring monthly mgmt fees; $54B->$73B by 2030 (~5% CAGR); top 2 only ~11% (best-in-class fragmentation). DECISIVE off-scorecard edge: co-lead Guillermo Lavergne (Ashford) is HOA domain expert + property mgmt already in PPM + women-led network CONFIRMED (CAI Long Island chapter woman-presided; CAI Womens Leadership Cmte; ~46pct mgmt-co CEOs women). Margin caveat: under 15pct sub-scale, 20-30pct at scale. PE roll-up 2022+ bids $1M+ EBITDA to 8-10x; sub-$1M off-market ~2-4x. KEY RISK: contracts cancellable 30-60d; trust-account controls (bring CPA). Channel = warm/CAI + Guillermo, NOT DealsX. One-pager+scorecard in Drive WEEKLY REVIEW.
Commercial/Industrial Air Purification Installed-Base Service and Compliance Maintenance
Likely eligible if acquired as a domestic C-corp service business; confirm tax counsel and watch equipment/manufacturing mix.
100-300 likely independently owned U.S. targets after excluding manufacturers, HVAC-only contractors, PE-backed platforms, product-only distributors, and subscale filter routes.

Score 2.44/3.00. TEST. Strong installed-base service thesis with market growth and target density; main diligence is contracted/repeat service mix versus install/equipment resale, plus PE heat. Folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1cs20XcJiEy4NJexAdlyYwR0JoFbvw20E. One-pager: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1QeTkNjrJHqsIFhNAvz7SIPVnRlZXYaUn/edit. Scorecard: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1XYW7BYW08hriupby_K7rwQ5N9eJUqq1y/edit.
Extremely fragmented; 1000+ deals since 2021. Many small owner-run janitorial/maintenance firms. PE reaching down into local/regional.

Janitorial/cleaning/maintenance under contract to commercial buildings. Recurring auto-renewing contracts, sticky, cycle-resilient. PE: LONG-STANDING + intensifying (ABM since 1990s; The Facilities Group/Greenbriar; Pye-Barker/Atlas; deal vol doubled 2018-22). Reaches DOWN into small firms more than HOA/PM. MULTIPLES: small owner-run 1.5-2.6x SDE (3-4.5x EBITDA); mid $1M+ 5-8x; janitorial hist mean ~8x (platform-skewed); large platforms 15x+ (exit only). Hard services (HVAC/fire) pricier than soft (janitorial). WEAKNESS: thin labor-heavy margins, wage inflation/turnover. Cheap lane: sub-$1M owner-run janitorial 2-4x SDE.
50-150+ if scoped to medical/lab/cleanroom/GMP specialty cleaning; IVF-only target pool likely thin

Specialized healthcare/lab/cleanroom cleaning with infection-control and contamination-control tailwinds. 2.37/3.00. Distinct from generic commercial cleaning if scoped to medical-office/ASC/lab/GMP protocols; IVF-only appears too thin. Validate 50+ buy-box-scale independents and margin premium before sprint activation. One-pager: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1HZdVFADRhG7kJwAclwPRyjMRwUAQ4nM9/edit?usp=drivesdk. Scorecard: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1RAavtMULjIsOqoDMp_y9c7XRXGloOVGx/edit?usp=drivesdk.

300+ US/Canada reserve-study firms (mostly small/independent) + NY-metro FISP/facade engineering long tail. Named: The Falcon Group (NJ), Merritt Engineering (NY), SUPERSTRUCTURES (NYC), Criterium-Hardy. No women-owned confirmed yet.

Reserve studies + building condition assessments + NYC FISP/Local Law 11 facade inspections (mandated 5-yr cycle, Cycle 10 2025-2030) for condos/HOAs/multifamily. Legally-RECURRING demand. PE: early innings - Reserve Advisors (Bel Air Growth Partners) rolling up (Browning 2024, Waldman 2026) but small end still cheap/below radar (~4-5x small vs 12-13x scaled). Margins 10-20pct. RISK: pure reserve-study TAM likely SUB-$500M (fails Growth-TAM gate unless defined broadly w/ FISP/structural inspection); QEWI licensed-engineer key-person dependence. Post-Surfside mandate tailwind. MAYBE.
Broker-Dealer Compliance and Outsourced FinOp Services
50-150 estimated outsourced FinOp/compliance providers; narrower buy-box pool likely 20-75 after excluding law firms/software/solo advisors

Score 2.34/3.00. Mandatory FINRA/SEC compliance burden; recurring outsourced FinOp/CCO/AML/testing retainers; current M&A signal via CRC-Oyster/MRS and ACA/FINOP Consulting. Red flags: finite broker-dealer universe, licensed senior-talent/key-person risk, financial-services QSBS uncertainty, compliance-platform consolidation. Folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1M4oV0qplNjFuIefs39Y4Bh0nAXf9H3QL

Score 2.33/3 (78%). Identifier flagged THIN-POOL CAVEAT (not target count - that is 50-200): SINGLE-SOURCE signal (Helen Guo SMB Deal Hunter 5/26), NO documented G&B/Kay network access into NATSA/trucking-compliance specialists, TAM extrapolated. Margins Medium / Recurring High / AI Defensibility Medium / RTW None / Network Access None. Drive: 1XnUD0ylZ-N_NRwBnNNWzrzjDpD-sbPBe
Outsourced Insurance SIU and Fraud Investigation Services
75-200 independent insurance-specialized PI/SIU/fraud investigation providers nationally; buy-box-scale platform pool unproven

Score 2.32/3.00. Carrier and TPA fraud leakage plus state SIU requirements create repeat panel/vendor demand; July 2026 Command/CoventBridge transaction and Ethos roll-up validate exit. Red flags: field-labor utilization, carrier panel concentration, multi-state PI licensing, larger claims-service platforms. Folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1tSc0SnS21br0aUr36rEa96P9_eBWXJwg
CMMC / FAR Managed Compliance Services for SMB Federal Contractors
Likely QSBS-eligible for advisory/managed services; confirm no software/platform-heavy structure.

Best regulatory/compliance fit of the three, with high growth and retainer conversion path. Main risks are policy timing, cyber/MSP crowding, and weak proprietary G&B network. Folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1PVFR6JymQ8WZcAHaPNNaob55MBKhz758
Geotechnical Engineering & Construction Materials Testing for Infrastructure/Commercial Construction
50+ likely nationally; exact deduped target count pending

Passes initial screen; promising infrastructure/commercial QA adjacency with ~$9B geotech TAM, ~$2B material-testing TAM, 3-6% growth, deal signal at ~$1M EBITDA on >$3.6M revenue. Advance only after target-discovery validates 50+ acquirable regional geotech/CMT/special inspection firms and repeat-revenue quality. Watch cyclicality, licensed labor, and E&O risk. One-pager: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1oU08ske_pU3r4hGcZKNR0zGvv3Yfmqqt/edit?usp=drivesdk. Scorecard: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1InaIkTuA4LCjqBBpZOdT1SHeAdLTUIvH/edit?usp=drivesdk.
Premium Physical Security Integration & Lifecycle Maintenance for Luxury Retail and Class-A Commercial Portfolios
50-150 luxury-retail/Class-A specialists inside 700-1,000+ independent integrators estimated.

Score 77/100 (2.31/3). Strong growth/TAM and recurring revenue potential via RMR, managed services, maintenance, and retrofit work. One-pager: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1_j4FgLvyrEN7to_XMStldqqyzFpmAqz4/edit?usp=drivesdk. Scorecard: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1zrs07_XCVczFw1RBq_p6HtwZ3-HXkDUt/edit?usp=drivesdk. Red flags: high PE saturation, mixed margins, project-heavy installer risk, vendor dependence, luxury/Class-A wedge unproven.

Wholesale DISTRIBUTION layer (annuity/life FMO/IMO override economics) — distinct from retail brokerage #7/#10/#13. Very-high capital-light margins, High recurring overrides, ~5-7% CAGR (annuity wave $464B 2025 sales). 4/4 initial screen PASS. PROBE-GATED: thin named-target pool (single historical source, no live target) — advance as one-pager + target-discovery probe before channel commitment. Consolidators Integrity/AmeriLife/Simplicity = play mid/small tier. Watch carrier disintermediation.
Surplus Lines Compliance & Tax Filing Services
RESURFACE (scored 2.65 on 3/21, never promoted). $129.8B E\&S premium, 12.4% filings growth. 10-20 indies after Vertafore/ReSource Pro roll-ups. Pairs w/ active Property Tax Appeal niche.
Art-Dealer Cultural-Goods Compliance and Back-Office Operations
Likely eligible only if a clean standalone domestic service company is acquired; law/CPA practices, partnerships, and embedded departments may not fit.
10-40 U.S.-reachable candidates; 40-120 global; heavy exclusions for law/CPA divisions, software-only tools, solo consultants, and pure advisors.

Score 1.96/3.00. HOLD. Strong art/luxury right-to-win and regulatory tailwind, but prove 20+ standalone targets and recurring-retainer economics before outreach. Folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1pnJthlCdJREb5tyrWRRhqnuO6KJOKkjf. One-pager: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1yjbQG2zS5uq1pmjY33tUzHCFxIz0cNh4/edit. Scorecard: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1mXrWs_GamCdbxRYq3Fx6_ICAvha9aiWt/edit.

Dozens of NYC-metro independents (Burnham, Nexus, Boyd, FNA Eng, JCA, Sol Building). Thousands of individual approved expeditors but few buy-box-scale firms. No women-owned confirmed (check NYC M/WBE).

NYC filing reps / permit expediting + zoning/land-use for developers. Margins healthy (10-20pct, comps 8.8-10.3x EBITDA). FAILS 2 buy-box gates: (1) NO contracted recurring (project/construction-cycle, relationship-repeat only); (2) HEAVILY PE-SATURATED - Milrose (Southfield) rolled up 14 firms since 2019, sold to Littlejohn 2026 (PE-to-PE exit), actively hunting exact NYC independents a searcher wants. Cloudpermit/Riverside on software side. ~$1.2-1.4B TAM (marginal). NY pain real but WEAK - open only via proprietary warm women-led NYC firm Milrose has not reached.
Dozens of independents (enterprise tier owned by JLL/CBRE/Colliers). Named: RE BackOffice (WOMAN-OWNED/NWBOC), Scribcor Global, National Lease Advisors, CREModels. NY-metro independents not surfaced.

Outsourced lease abstraction + CAM/opex reconciliation + ASC 842 lease accounting + RE bookkeeping. Margins 10-20pct (offshore arbitrage), partial recurring (admin/CAM recurring, abstraction project), REMOTE-friendly (WFH fit). NOT PE-saturated as pure-play BUT for a BAD reason: AI abstraction is EXISTENTIAL margin threat - $150-300/lease manual & $50-100 offshore collapsing to ~$20 automated (70-90pct labor cut). Melting ice cube. WOMAN-OWNED target (RE BackOffice). WEAK - fails the AI-disruptable exclude unless target is stickier CAM-recovery/admin-heavy, not abstraction volume.

B2B, recurring compliance-driven service revenue (pads/batteries/inspections), regulatory tailwind (expanding AED mandates), highly fragmented, low AI-disruption, female operator. Almost nobody is chasing this.

Few hundred independent regional firms US; NY-metro cluster. Named: Think Utility Services (NY 60+yr), Oates Energy (NY), Bay City Metering (NYC/NJ/CT), Synergy, Anchor Utility. No women-owned confirmed.

Submeter install (one-time capex) + recurring monthly per-unit billing fees (~$3-7/unit, SaaS-like, sticky). Margins 15-25pct (billing-heavy), TAM $2.8-4.4B, growth 8-11pct CAGR. STRONG recurring BUT HEAVILY PE-SATURATED (the problem): TPG/Conservice (~25pct share), RealPage, Metergy/Brookfield, Zego/Global Payments - roll-up crossfire. Small NY end cheaper (5-9x) but actively hunted bolt-on fodder; PMS (RealPage/Yardi) bundle-encroach below ~100K units. WEAK/MAYBE - good business, saturated market. Viable only as defensible single-metro NY water-submetering play, exit-to-strategic.

Niche-intelligence Tuesday lane. Asset-light firms that collect water/soil/air samples, manage chain-of-custody, coordinate accredited lab work, and write compliance reports for municipalities, developers, property owners, industrial facilities, restoration projects, and environmental engineers. First question: is the buy-box-scale target pool real, or mostly large firms plus subscale specialists? Kay wedge: environmental sampling internship + science research/Westinghouse credibility.
